title: DP fundamentals
learn: overlapping subproblems + optimal substructure, memoization (top-down, `@cache`) vs tabulation (bottom-up), state + transition + base case, space optimization
hook: DP scares people more than any other topic, but it's just recursion that remembers its answers. Climbing Stairs is the question interviewers use to see whether you can go from a brute-force recursion to O(n).

explain.prompt: Explain dynamic programming using Climbing Stairs: the recurrence, why plain recursion is slow, and how memoization and tabulation fix it.
keyPoints: define the state: dp[i] = number of ways to reach step i
recurrence from the last choice: dp[i] = dp[i − 1] + dp[i − 2], with base cases dp[0] = dp[1] = 1
plain recursion recomputes the same subproblems: O(2ⁿ)
memoization caches each answer (top-down); tabulation fills a table from the base cases (bottom-up): O(n)
only the last two values are needed, so O(1) space is possible
